title: Remove a stroller rear wheel for axle and hub servicing
instruction: Remove the stroller rear wheel so its axle and wheel hub can be serviced. The frame is already safely supported in the bench clamp. Hold the lower release lever, support the full-size wheel while withdrawing its steel axle completely, and put the wheel upright in the empty maintenance rack. Release the lever and both hands, leaving the wheel stable and the spring retainer returned. Cleaning or refitting the wheel is a subsequent operation, not part of this task.
context: Parents and repair workers remove pushchair wheels to access the axle and hub during maintenance. The Britax B-AGILE owner guide (printed p7, https://csus.britax.com/media/7460/p590000b_b-agile-ug_low-res-web.pdf) documents holding the bottom release lever while drawing the rear wheel away. This bounded task performs that removal and stable workshop storage; it does not claim cleaning, repair, reinstallation or roadworthiness inspection.
setup: Stock calibrated bimanual YAM station with unchanged bodies, collision meshes, drives and grippers. Coordinates are metres: +x forward, +y left, +z above the 0.7475 m tabletop. Left/right arm bases are (0,+/-0.305,0.0025) in this frame. Each starts at joint angles [0,1,1,-0.6,0,0] rad with gripper 1 (open). Actions are 14 absolute joint/jaw targets at 20 Hz. Policy input is 320x176 RGB from top_cam, left_cam and right_cam plus the actual 14 joint/jaw values; side_cam is review only. Native CPU PhysX runs at 240 Hz; RTX provides rendering. A molded-rim wheel with a rubber/foam tire is 240 mm in diameter, 38 mm wide and 580 g. The 12 mm steel spindle is 121 mm long and 110 g; it has an 8 mm root-diameter, 5 mm wide annular groove and a 5 mm tapered end. Wheel and spindle body origins both start at (0.360,0,0.150), identity orientation, axle along +x, joined by an unrestricted revolute bearing. Their receiver has two physical lands forming a 12.6 mm bore from x=0.420 to 0.485 at y=0,z=0.150. The 25 g steel spring retainer starts at (0.445,0,0.134); its colored pull tab is 18x18x12 mm, centered at (0.445,0.052,0.128). Its vertical guide allows 8 mm downward travel, with a constant 400 N/m spring, 2 Ns/m damping and 1 mm preload target. The frame module is already safely bench-clamped: a 110x140x12 mm clamp base is centered at (0.530,0,0.006), with a 40x40x170 mm aluminum frame leg at (0.530,0,0.097) and a rigid hub receiver. The empty rigid maintenance rack is centered at (0.510,-0.245), with a 66x270x4 mm base, 43 mm internal axial clearance, 90 mm cheeks and 10 mm tire saddles. Its nominal wheel-center datum is (0.510,-0.245,0.131). All task-body velocities start at zero. One wheel and one empty rack are present; no replacement wheel is included. Hardware materials, dimensions, masses and spring values are engineering estimates. All custom geometry is generated by tools/build_assets.py.
scoring: Observe actual native poses, velocities and robot-to-task contacts every 240 Hz step. Require a physical retainer retraction beyond 1.8 mm before axle withdrawal; the actual far spindle tip must clear the receiver front by 8 mm. Final wheel center must be within 6/12/9 mm in x/y/z of its rack datum, with its actual wheel axis x component above 0.995. Wheel and spindle speeds must be below 10 mm/s, wheel angular speed below 0.25 rad/s, retainer returned within 0.3 mm and every robot-task contact absent. Require these conditions continuously for one elapsed second, meaning at least 241 consecutive native samples. Invalid/nonfinite state, nonunit orientation, bearing or slider-guide separation, withdrawal before release, work-area departure or a wheel below the bench void the trial. Score 0 initially or invalid, 0.25 after release, 0.5 after complete withdrawal, 0.75 after upright rack placement, 1.0 only at the complete released stable endpoint. Only 1.0 is success.
fidelity: Full-size wheel, spring-tip/groove, open receiver bore, free bearing and tire-supported rack. Geometry, hollow-assembly mass, friction and spring settings are engineering estimates, without OEM CAD or hardware calibration. No tire deformation, dirt, wear or manufacturing variation. Supported rear-hub module only; whole-stroller and passenger handling excluded. Native contact and constant passive spring; no task motor, proximity latch, attachment, body teleport or verification force.
reset_notes: Restore only the three task-body poses and zero velocities at episode reset; return the unchanged robot to READY. Thereafter native contact, gravity, the fixed passive spring and ordinary robot actions determine task motion. Fixed hub module and rack remain secured to the bench. Scripted development reference has privileged read-only simulator access; standard policy observation remains three RGB images and actual robot joint/jaw positions.
scores: Scripted: 1.0 in 604/700 actions, two fresh fixed-start trials. Dream-1 beta: 0.0 in 700/700 actions, one fixed-start trial; 14 successful chunks in 27 attempts. Native grades and model inputs replayed exactly. No hardware validation or external submission.
